exercise.name: Lying Alternate Straight Leg Circle
aliases: Lying leg circles (one leg at a time)

reference.title: Lying Alternate Straight Leg Circle
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; page could not be read at authoring time, movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (hip circumduction with the knee straight, trunk held)

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily through each circle; exhale as the leg lifts.
breathing.cadence: One circle in about 2.4 s, then switch legs

prescription.progression: Bigger circles, then lower the circle closer to the floor, then add an ankle weight

cues.text: Lie flat, arms by your sides palms down, legs long.
Brace and raise the straight right leg to about 45 degrees.
Draw a smooth circle with the toes: across, down, out and up. The pelvis stays still.
Lower the leg to the mat under control.
Repeat with the left leg: same size circle, same direction.
Rest briefly; reverse the direction on the next set.

mistakes.mistake: Pelvis rocking side to side with the leg
mistakes.fix: Make the circle smaller and press the arms into the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching off the mat
mistakes.fix: Raise the circle higher or bend the resting knee with the foot flat.

mistakes.mistake: Knee bending to make the circle bigger
mistakes.fix: Keep the knee long; the circle comes from the hip.
Slow, even circles about 2-3 seconds each.

kinematics.norm: About 30-60 degrees for the circle centre (clinical opinion)
Circle spans about 30 degrees of flexion (clinical opinion)
Circle crosses slightly past the midline and out about 15 degrees (clinical opinion)
Pelvis stays on the mat (clinical opinion; McGill 1998 for straight-leg loading)

kinematics.peak: One circle in 2.4 s per leg, lower 0.6 s
kinematics.norm: Slow circles, about 2-3 s each (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #15155, Lying Alternate Straight Leg Circle, video (movement reference)
Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)
Juker, McGill et al. 1998, Intramuscular psoas and abdominal EMG (Med Sci Sports Exerc)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Straight-leg and legs-off-the-floor work loads the low back through the hip flexors (McGill 1998). If the low back arches off the mat, bend the knees or shorten the range.
Low-back pain or disc problems: prefer dead bugs or bent-knee alternatives.
modify: Bend the resting knee with the foot flat on the mat.
progressions: Lower the circle toward the floor.

muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris hold the straight leg up and steer the flexion part of the circle (Juker 1998 for psoas in leg raising).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Same role on the left leg in the second half.
muscleNotes.core: The abdominals hold the pelvis still against the one-sided pull of the leg; unilateral leg lifts need less abdominal effort than bilateral ones (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Pull the leg across the midline in the inner part of the circle (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Takes the leg out to the side in the outer part of the circle (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the pelvis rolling with the leg.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the pelvis rolling with the leg.
